reason: E2 supports sigma phase formation at grain boundaries above ~950 K and associated property reduction, but it does not mention the specific alloy, oxidation-driven segregation of Ti/Al/Cr, or oxide precipitates. E1 discusses corrosion in different HEAs and media, providing no direct support for any of the key premises. The core mechanistic claims about oxidation-induced segregation and embrittlement are therefore largely unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Reactive elements (Ti, Al, Cr) segregate to grain boundaries during high-temperature exposure in this specific HEA.
This segregation leads to formation of brittle oxide-based precipitates or intermetallic/sigma-like phases at grain boundaries.
These grain-boundary precipitates drastically impair intergranular cohesion and cause catastrophic failure.
In reducing environments, the absence of oxide films suppresses this pathway but alternative phase changes may still weaken the material.
The sigma phase preferentially forms at grain boundaries above ~950 K and reduces mechanical properties.
